title: Wooden spoon
scenario: Announce the LOWEST score (the wooden spoon).

intro.job: Announce the LOWEST score (the wooden spoon).

idea.rule: Same line-up, other end — smallest first means the spoon is at the FRONT.
idea.detail: sort() lines the scores up smallest first. The best is at the end, [-1]; the lowest is at the front, [0].

model_restatement: Find the lowest score and print it.

clarify.question: What if two scores tie for lowest?
What if there are no scores?
Can I use min()?
clarify.answer: min() would do it — here, use sort so we can watch the line-up.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Sort the scores, take the one at the end, and announce it.

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — after line 2, what is spoon?

why_line: After sort(), the end of the line is the BIGGEST score — scores[-1] hands the spoon to 87.

explain.rule: Smallest first means the end of the line is the trophy, not the spoon — scores[-1] grabs the winner.
explain.bridge: So which end of the line is the lowest score standing at?

fix.rule: After sort(), the lowest is at the front — scores[0].

alternatives.note: min() skips the sort — the shortcut.

hints: After line 1, which score is at the end?
sort() is smallest first. The spoon is at the other end.

follow_up.prompt: A tie at the top: [9, 9, 1] — who gets the spoon?
follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — sorted, the lowest is still at the front.

one_liner: Same line-up, other end — smallest first means the spoon is at the FRONT.
